subject: Re: Production regression after model update / rollback & pinning plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-28T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: model behaviour change observed (ACME)

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we can move fast: 

Summary of concern
- ACME noticed a quality regression starting Feb 25 after the default model for your endpoint moved from redwood-qa-v2.0 to redwood-qa-v2.1. Outputs are shorter and less consistent on the product-summarization prompt set.

What I have from our call
- Impact: CI alert triggered on 4 of 12 critical prompt checks; some production requests returned incomplete summaries.
- Triage so far: your team uploaded the prompt examples to our support case. You gave us permission to run diffs between v2.0 and v2.1 on the ACME prompt set.

Next steps (proposed)
1) Please attach a small sample of failing requests + expected outputs (you mentioned ~30 examples).
2) With your permission we will run an automated diff (redwood internal tool) to identify where logits/decoding diverged and whether the change is in tokenization, decoding defaults, or model weight delta.
3) If the regression is material for production we can pin your route to redwood-qa-v2.0 while engineers complete a root-cause analysis and either patch v2.1 or provide a tuned variant.

Let me know if I missed anything — also sharing the benchmark and prompt-set links below so you have them in one place.

Links attached: benchmarks_acme_202602.pdf, prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model behaviour change observed (ACME)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap. Confirming we saw the first production regression on Feb 25 and it’s been intermittent but customer-facing. I attached the sample we discussed (acme_failing_examples.csv).

Priority
- We need a mitigation ASAP. If pinning to v2.0 is a 1–2 hour operation, we’d like to request that today. Our SRE is standing by to swap traffic if you need a target.

What we included in the CSV
- Request id, prompt snippet, actual output, expected output, timestamp.

Please let us know the earliest ETA for pin/rollback and if you need any more examples.

—Sarah
Head of Platform Engineering | ACME Corp
platform@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT: ACME - regression after auto-upgrade to redwood-qa-v2.1 (samples attached)

Team — looping you in based on today’s call + sample from ACME. They reported production-quality regressions after the auto-upgrade to v2.1. They’ve asked for a rollback/pin if we can do it quickly.

Attachments: acme_failing_examples.csv, prompt_set_acme_v1.jsonl, benchmarks_acme_202602.pdf

Key asks from ACME- Rollback/pin to v2.0 on their live route as an immediate mitigation (they asked for 1–2 hours ETA).- Run a prioritized diff against the 30 sample prompts + our internal benchmarks to confirm whether the regression is due to model weights vs decoding defaults.

Recommended approach (proposed)
1) Engineering: run the automated model diff tool against the attached prompt_set_acme_v1 (link: https://internal.redwood/dev/diffs/redwood-qa-v2.1-vs-v2.0).
2) Support: prepare a canary pin (route-level override) for ACME so traffic can be switched in <2h if needed.
3) Product/Eng: if diff shows weight-level regressions that change semantics, propose a temporary roll-forward to a tuned variant or patch. If it’s decoding defaults, we can patch config and test in staging.

ETA asks
- Can we get a quick feasibility and ETA from infra/serving on the pin operation?
- Can we get an initial diff summary in ~4 business hours so we can update ACME?

Sarah — I’ll keep you posted. Internal, please reply with ETA.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: ACME - regression after auto-upgrade to redwood-qa-v2.1 (samples attached)

Marissa / team — quick update from serving/infra after running the diff on the ACME prompt set and internal benchmarks: 

Findings (initial)
- The automated diff shows consistent token-level distribution shifts across ~65% of failing prompts; changes align with a softmax temperature tweak and a small weight delta in the final LM head between v2.0 and v2.1.
- We do not see a tokenizer change. Decoding config defaults for v2.1 tightened max_new_tokens and nucleus sampling p by default which explains shorter outputs in many cases.

Recommended mitigation (short-term)
1) Pin ACME's route to redwood-qa-v2.0 (we have an existing pinned artifact: redwood-qa-v2.0-p202602). This is a quick route override and will be live within ~30–60 minutes once we get ACME SRE confirmation to cut traffic.
2) Create a canary with v2.0 pinned for 10% traffic for 1h to validate behavior, then switch to 100% if green.

Recommended long-term
- We will prepare a patched v2.1 variant that restores the previous decoding defaults and toally verify head-weight impact; target is a patch release (v2.1.1) in ~5 business days if no additional regressions surface.

Action items
- Marissa: confirm to ACME that we can pin now and request their SRE to confirm time for traffic switch.
- Monica: please open an internal runbook ticket and include the diff link (https://internal.redwood/dev/diffs/redwood-qa-v2.1-vs-v2.0) and attach the ACME CSV.
- Rishi/Eng: start the patch branch for v2.1.1 focused on decoding defaults and LM head checks.

I’ll post the full diff report to the ticket in ~2 hours.

—Aditya
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
